title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 64
paragraphs: So satisfaction for the murder of Leonidas was paid by Mardonius, according to the oracle given to the Spartans; and the most famous victory known to us was won by Pausanias son of Cleombrotos, son of Anaxandrides, whose earlier ancestors have been named in connection with Leonidas, since as it happens they are the same for both. Now Mardonius was killed by Arimnestos, a man of standing in Sparta, who afterwards, when the Median wars were over, with three hundred men fought a battle against the entire Messenian army then at war with the Lacedaemonians, at Stenycleros; and both he was killed and the three hundred along with him.
